## Recall · Lecture 2

a) A phone has 8 cores at 3 GHz. How fast is one core?
b) Which part keeps the saves when the power is off?
c) How many MB is 4 GB?

::: {.answer}
a) 3 GHz
b) the storage
c) 4096 MB
:::

## Check 1 · Parts and four lines

What does a good spec sheet of the lab computer show?

::: {.reveal}
1. The processor line gives the name, the cores and the GHz, for example Core i5, 6 cores, up to 4.4 GHz.
2. The memory line gives the RAM, for example 16 GB.
3. The storage line gives the drive, for example 512 GB SSD.
4. The graphics line says whether the GPU is inside the processor or on a card.
:::

- **Do it:** Choose a laptop with two reasons. Why can the game not go on L2, which has "256 GB"?
- Your product is a choice with two reasons.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/memory-hierarchy.png)

## Check 2 · Choose and explain

Which laptop is right for the game, and why?

::: {.reveal}
1. Only L1 has the 16 GB of RAM that the game needs.
2. Only L1 has more than 60 GB free: it has 120 GB.
3. So the studio chooses L1, which also has faster cores.
4. L2 has a capacity of 256 GB, but only 40 GB of it is free.
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can name the main parts of a computer and write its spec sheet.
- You can choose a device for a game from its cores, RAM and free storage.
